national.name: FEMA Individual Assistance (IA)
national.desc: Federal disaster assistance for homeowners and renters in federally declared disaster areas. Covers temporary housing, home repair, and other disaster-related expenses. This is NOT a grant for historic preservation: home repair assistance only makes the home safe, sanitary, or functional. The maximum award is set each year by the disaster's declaration date (for example, $44,800 for housing assistance for disasters declared on or after October 1, 2025; a newer notice may apply to later disasters).
national.desc_es: Asistencia federal por desastre para propietarios e inquilinos en áreas declaradas como zona de desastre federal. Cubre vivienda temporal, reparación del hogar y otros gastos relacionados con el desastre. NO es una subvención para preservación histórica: la asistencia para reparación del hogar solo deja la vivienda segura, salubre o funcional. El monto máximo se fija cada año según la fecha de declaración del desastre (por ejemplo, $44,800 para asistencia de vivienda en desastres declarados a partir del 1 de octubre de 2025; para desastres posteriores puede aplicar un aviso más reciente).
national.note: Historic property owners: tell FEMA your home is historic (listed on or eligible for the National Register, or in a historic district). FEMA's IA grants are subject to historic preservation review. But FEMA home repair money only makes a home safe, sanitary, or functional, priced at average quality. It does not pay for historic-quality materials or restoration, so look to insurance, an SBA loan, and preservation programs for the difference. Talk to your SHPO before removing historic material.
national.note_es: Propietarios de propiedades históricas: informe a FEMA que su vivienda es histórica (inscrita o elegible para el Registro Nacional, o dentro de un distrito histórico). Las subvenciones de Asistencia Individual de FEMA están sujetas a revisión de preservación histórica. Pero el dinero de FEMA para reparación solo deja la vivienda segura, salubre o funcional, calculado con materiales de calidad promedio. No paga materiales de calidad histórica ni restauración, así que busque la diferencia en su seguro, un préstamo de la SBA y los programas de preservación. Consulte a su SHPO antes de retirar material histórico.
sources: FEMA IAPPG v1.1 Amended (docs/fema-iappg-v1.1-amended-2025.pdf) p.14: Federally-funded IA grants and programs are subject to compliance with EHP compliance requirements, including... the National Historic Preservation Act.
FEMA IAPPG v1.1 Amended (docs/fema-iappg-v1.1-amended-2025.pdf) p.86: Home Repair Assistance is intended to make the damaged home safe, sanitary, or functional.

FEMA IAPPG v1.1 Amended (docs/fema-iappg-v1.1-amended-2025.pdf) p.89: Home Repair Assistance award amounts are based on repair or replacement of components that are of average quality, size, or capacity.

Federal Register 2026-19854, 91 FR 61429 (Sept 29, 2026): maximum ... is $44,800 for housing assistance and $44,800 for other needs assistance ... for any single emergency or major disaster declared on or after October 1, 2025. https://www.federalregister.gov/d/2026-19854

national.name: SBA Disaster Loans — Home & Personal Property
national.name_es: Préstamos por Desastre SBA — Hogar y Propiedad Personal
national.desc: Low-interest federal loans to repair or replace disaster-damaged property: homeowners can apply for up to $500,000 for a primary residence, and homeowners and renters for up to $100,000 for personal property. Must be in a declared disaster area. This is a loan, NOT a grant — repayment required.
national.desc_es: Préstamos federales de bajo interés para reparar o reemplazar propiedad dañada por desastre: los propietarios pueden solicitar hasta $500,000 para su residencia principal, y propietarios e inquilinos hasta $100,000 para bienes personales. Debe estar en un área declarada de desastre. Es un préstamo, NO una subvención — se requiere reembolso.
national.note: If FEMA refers you to SBA, complete the SBA application even if you don't want a loan. FEMA can help with personal property, vehicles, and group flood insurance only if SBA turns you down or lends too little. If you withdraw your application or decline an SBA loan, FEMA won't consider those needs again. FEMA home repair grants don't depend on SBA.
national.note_es: Si FEMA lo refiere a la SBA, complete la solicitud de la SBA aunque no quiera un préstamo. FEMA solo puede ayudar con bienes personales, vehículos y el seguro grupal contra inundaciones si la SBA le niega el préstamo o le presta menos de lo necesario. Si retira su solicitud o rechaza un préstamo de la SBA, FEMA no volverá a considerar esas necesidades. Las subvenciones de FEMA para reparación del hogar no dependen de la SBA.
national.apply: Apply at SBA Disaster Loan Assistance portal
sources: https://www.sba.gov/funding-programs/disaster-assistance/physical-damage-loans (fetched 2026-10-02): Homeowners may apply for up to $500,000 to replace or repair their primary residence. / Renters and homeowners may borrow up to $100,000 to replace or repair personal property

FEMA IAPPG v1.1 Amended (docs/fema-iappg-v1.1-amended-2025.pdf) p.46: Only applicants who do not qualify for a loan from the SBA may be eligible for assistance for the SBA-dependent category. / SBA-dependent ONA includes Personal Property Assistance, Transportation Assistance, and Group Flood Insurance Policy (GFIP).
FEMA IAPPG v1.1 Amended (docs/fema-iappg-v1.1-amended-2025.pdf) p.145: FEMA refers the applicant's information to SBA if the applicant's income meets SBA minimum guidelines.

FEMA IAPPG v1.1 Amended (docs/fema-iappg-v1.1-amended-2025.pdf) p.166: Applicants who withdraw from the process or decline a loan from the SBA will not be referred back to FEMA for assistance with SBA-Dependent ONA.
FEMA IAPPG v1.1 Amended (docs/fema-iappg-v1.1-amended-2025.pdf) p.44 vs p.46: Home Repair is Housing Assistance; the SBA-dependent list is ONA only.

national.name: NPS / SHPO Historic Preservation Programs
national.name_es: Programas de Preservación Histórica NPS / SHPO
national.desc: National Park Service preservation grants (via state SHPOs). When federal funds are involved (including FEMA assistance), Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act requires review of effects on buildings listed in or eligible for the National Register of Historic Places. Your building doesn't have to be listed: your State Historic Preservation Office (SHPO) can tell you whether it is eligible, and may know of technical assistance.
national.desc_es: Subvenciones de preservación del Servicio de Parques Nacionales (a través de las SHPO estatales). Cuando se usan fondos federales (incluida la asistencia de FEMA), la Sección 106 de la Ley Nacional de Preservación Histórica exige revisar cómo les afectan los trabajos a los edificios inscritos o elegibles para el Registro Nacional de Lugares Históricos. Su edificio no tiene que estar inscrito: su Oficina Estatal de Preservación Histórica (SHPO) puede decirle si es elegible y puede conocer programas de asistencia técnica.
national.note: Contact your SHPO early — they take part in Section 106 review with FEMA and can advise on preservation-sensitive repair approaches.
national.note_es: Contacte a su SHPO temprano: participa en la revisión de la Sección 106 con FEMA y puede orientarle sobre enfoques de reparación sensibles a la preservación.
national.apply: Contact your state SHPO (see state-specific programs above)
sources: FEMA PAPPG v5.0 Amended (docs/fema-pappg-v5.0-amended-2025.pdf) App. D p.275: Historic properties include buildings ... included in, or eligible for inclusion in, the National Register of Historic Places.

FEMA IAPPG v1.1 Amended (docs/fema-iappg-v1.1-amended-2025.pdf) App. G p.266: Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act requires FEMA to consider the effects a project will have on historic properties

VT.name: Vermont Division for Historic Preservation
VT.desc: Vermont SHPO can connect you with state preservation programs and FEMA-related historic building assistance. Eligible listed and contributing structures may qualify for additional review support.

VT.name: Vermont Emergency Relief and Assistance Fund (ERAF)
VT.desc: State fund that can supplement FEMA assistance for eligible Vermonters. Contact Vermont Emergency Management for current disaster declaration status.

NC.name: NC State Historic Preservation Office
NC.desc: SHPO can identify preservation grant programs and connect historic property owners with technical assistance for appropriate repair approaches.

NC.name: NC Emergency Management
NC.desc: State-level disaster assistance coordination, including Individual Assistance programs in federally declared disaster areas.

PR.name: Puerto Rico State Historic Preservation Office (SHPO)
PR.name_es: Oficina Estatal de Preservación Histórica de Puerto Rico (SHPO)
PR.desc: PR SHPO has an active NPS capacity-building grant and can provide assessment support, technical guidance, and connection to preservation programs for historic properties.
PR.desc_es: La SHPO de PR tiene una subvención activa de desarrollo de capacidad del NPS y puede proporcionar apoyo de evaluación, orientación técnica y conexión con programas de preservación para propiedades históricas.

PR.name: PR Emergency Management Bureau (NMEAD)
PR.name_es: Negociado de Manejo de Emergencias y Administración de Desastres (NMEAD)
PR.desc: Coordinates federal disaster assistance programs in Puerto Rico, including FEMA IA registration and state-level supplemental programs.
PR.desc_es: Coordina programas federales de asistencia por desastre en Puerto Rico, incluyendo el registro de FEMA IA y programas suplementarios a nivel estatal.
